implementationPlan.description:
THE RESOLVER - the piece that genuinely does not exist. Create `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-launch-resolver.ts` (+ a one-line `.js` bridge, the package convention).

It answers, for a launch: WHICH project, WHICH environment, and FOR WHAT PURPOSE - then calls the EXISTING `readEnvironmentDelivery(config, environment)` (environment-delivery.ts:104) and returns either the delivered variables or a refusal. It builds no store, no decoder and no second allowlist (rail 2); it is a resolver, not an authority.

PURPOSE IS A FIRST-CLASS INPUT, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT. Rail 1: "resolve intended project/environment and purpose at the real launch boundary, never broad process.env plus extras." A verifier run for environment `preview` and a coding seat are different purposes with different answers, and the type should make it impossible to ask for delivery without saying which.

THE CODING-SEAT PURPOSE RESOLVES TO NO DELIVERY, structurally rather than by convention - make it a case the type system forces the caller to handle, so a future call site cannot omit it and silently get production values.

REFUSALS: a scope mismatch or unavailable delivery refuses with the EXACT stable code and layer the environment module already defines (DoD 2), reusing an already-rostered layer literal. Introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant. AND THE REFUSAL CARRIES NO RAW ERROR DATA (DoD 2) - a store error message can quote a key or a value, so map it to a code rather than forwarding it.

`wc -l` and keep under 250.
implementationPlan.note:
THE RESOLVER. environment-launch-resolver.ts = 184 lines (cap 250, OK) + one-line .js bridge `export * from "./environment-launch-resolver.ts";` matching the convention in environment-delivery.js / environment-contracts.js.

RAIL 2 HELD - NO SECOND AUTHORITY. Imports only: environmentRefusal + isEnvironmentName + EnvironmentName/EnvironmentRefusal types (environment-contracts.js), readEnvironmentDelivery + EnvironmentDeliveredVariables (environment-delivery.js), EnvironmentStoreConfig type (environment-projection.js). No store opened, no record decoded, no second allowlist, no hand-rolled name list, no new *_LAYER constant.

PURPOSE IS A REQUIRED PARAMETER. LAUNCH_PURPOSES = ["CODING_SEAT","PREVIEW","VERIFIER"]. resolveEnvironmentLaunch(config, purpose) - a call site cannot ask for variables without first saying who receives them. PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS is total, closed and ONE-WAY: PREVIEW->"preview", VERIFIER->"verify", both members of ENVIRONMENT_NAMES (environment-contracts.ts:29), enforced by `satisfies Readonly<Record<string, EnvironmentName>>`. The caller does NOT get to name an environment, so a preview cannot ask for `production`.

DEPLOY DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the map, with the reason in the doc comment naming task-04b3ce7e. Adding a DEPLOY member would advertise a resolution no launch site can consume - it would READ as wired while nothing consumes it.

CODING SEAT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CONVENTIONAL. Two mechanisms, both compiler-enforced:
 (a) EnvironmentLaunchWithheld.delivered is `WithheldDelivery = Readonly<Record<string, never>>` - the value type is UNINHABITED, so `delivered["X"] = v` does not compile for ANY v. An empty object literal or a boolean flag would have relied on downstream memory; this cannot be grown into a delivering shape.
 (b) `environment: null` on the withheld branch vs `EnvironmentName` on the delivering one, so a caller that wants a value MUST narrow - isLaunchDelivered() is that narrowing, and the coding-seat case becomes visible rather than defaulted through.
 (c) Defence in depth: the CODING_SEAT branch returns the shared frozen WITHHELD **before the store is touched at all** and before the credential is ever resolved. There is no path from a coding-seat launch to a plaintext value even if the rest of the module is wrong.

REFUSALS - EXACT CODE AND LAYER, NO RAW ERROR DATA (DoD 2). Two distinct failure kinds, both handled:
 - A REFUSAL from readEnvironmentDelivery is FORWARDED UNCHANGED and UNRESTAMPED (`if (read.ok === false) return read;`). It already carries the rostered code AND the layer that answered: ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN@SCOPE for a scope mismatch, ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE@KEY for an underivable seal. Restamping would report KEY trouble as SCOPE trouble.
 - A THROW is caught and MAPPED to environmentRefusal("ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE"). This is the DoD-2 "without raw error data" clause and the reason it is not a passthrough: nothing under readEnvironmentDelivery promises not to throw, and a store failure's `message` can quote a key, a path or a value which would then ride the launch-failure log. environmentRefusal takes NO layer argument (environment-contracts.ts:100) and its detail is fixed prose keyed by code, so no call site can pair a wrong layer or attach its own message. Zero new codes, zero new layers.
 - Redundant SCOPE guard on the mapped environment name: harmless today (both values are in the roster), keeps the code SCOPE-layer if a future map member is misspelled instead of depending on a downstream check.

launchDelivery(config, purpose) is the launch-site convenience: returns `undefined` rather than `{}` when nothing is delivered, so deliverEnvironment (environment-delivery.ts:161) takes its identity branch and returns the caller's own object BY REFERENCE - the byte-identical no-op DoD 5 requires. A refusal also becomes `undefined`: a boundary that cannot read the store starts its child WITHOUT operator variables rather than not starting at all, the same still-running/fail-closed choice deliverEnvironment's header makes for a colliding name. A caller wanting to distinguish withheld from unreadable uses resolveEnvironmentLaunch and inspects the refusal.

PLANTED-ERROR CONTROL (green typecheck is worthless without proof the file is in the include set): appended `const PLANTED_CONTROL: number = "not a number";` -> `npx tsc --project tsconfig.json` from apps/daemon EXIT 1 with `src/environment/environment-launch-resolver.ts(186,7): error TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.` So the new module IS compiled by the daemon leg.
DRILL RESTORE PROOF: the file is UNTRACKED (`git status --porcelain` = `?? apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-launch-resolver.ts`), so git diff certifies NOTHING for it. Backed up out of tree to %TEMP%/elr-worker-adefb11e.bak BEFORE mutating; restored by copy; prove

implementationPlan.description:
COMPOSE IT AT THE BOUNDARIES STEP 1 FOUND REAL - and NOT at the coding-seat call sites.

For each in-scope boundary (verifier in agent-wrapper-main.ts, preview in the preview runner, deploy only if step 1 found a production caller), resolve the project/environment/purpose and pass the result as `agentEnvironment`'s second argument, or through `deliverEnvironment` where the merge's collision report is wanted.

LEAVE agent-spawner.ts:156 AND :159 ONE-ARGUMENT. This is the row's single most important negative requirement. Those are the CODING SEAT call sites; passing `delivered` there would hand every agent the project's production secrets, which rail 1 forbids and DoD 3 names. The optional parameter on `agentEnvironment` exists so a specific boundary can OPT IN - it is not an invitation for the general spawner. If a change to agent-spawner.ts seems necessary, it is to thread a purpose through, never to supply delivery by default.

USE THE COLLISION REPORT. `deliverEnvironment` (:153) returns collisions between the allowlisted host environment and the delivered values; decide what a collision means at each boundary and say so in the note. Silently letting a delivered value win over a host value - or the reverse - is a decision either way, and an undocumented one becomes a debugging problem during an incident.

EXISTING CALLERS MUST STAY BYTE-IDENTICAL. `agentEnvironment`'s comment states that an absent `delivered` yields a byte-identical environment; step 6 asserts that for the untouched paths.

implementationPlan.description:
THE RESOLVER'S ARMS (DoD 2) - `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-launch-resolver.test.ts`.

(a) THE SELECTED ENVIRONMENT'S VALUE ARRIVES: a child intended for environment X receives X's value, not another environment's. Assert with two environments configured so a resolver that ignores the selector cannot pass.
(b) THE CLOSED ALLOWLIST STILL EXCLUDES AMBIENT HOST VARIABLES: set a non-allowlisted variable in the source environment and assert it is ABSENT from the result. `agentEnvironment` applies `delivered` LAST to a roster-filtered object, so this arm proves the roster still governs the host half.
(c) A CODING-SEAT PURPOSE RESOLVES TO NO DELIVERY - assert zero delivered variables, not merely that the call succeeded. This is DoD 3's negative half at the unit level.
(d) SCOPE MISMATCH and UNAVAILABLE DELIVERY each refuse with the EXACT stable code AND the layer that refused - never merely that it failed.
(e) NO RAW ERROR DATA IN A REFUSAL (DoD 2): drive the store to fail with an error whose message contains a distinctive sentinel, and assert that sentinel is ABSENT from the refusal. Store errors quote keys and sometimes values; forwarding one is how a value escapes through an error path.

MUTATE AND CONFIRM RED for (c): make the coding-seat purpose fall through to delivery and confirm the arm reds; restore and prove it. That file is new and untracked, so back it up out of tree and prove the restore by SHA256 in a separate call.
implementationPlan.note:
10 ARMS, ALL GREEN. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=2 --testTimeout=30000 environment-launch-resolver` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 10 passed (10)`, EXIT 0. Nonzero executed count, so not vacuous.

(a) SELECTED ENVIRONMENT'S VALUE ARRIVES. All THREE environments seeded with the SAME name (DATABASE_URL) and DIFFERENT values, so a resolver ignoring its selector returns something present, well-formed and WRONG - which a single-environment fixture cannot detect. VERIFIER gets the verify value, PREVIEW gets the preview value, and the negative half asserts neither can see the other's value NOR `production`'s (the environment a scope confusion lands on and the one holding real operator secrets).

ROSTER ARM, BOTH DIRECTIONS (global rail). Iterating LAUNCH_PURPOSES alone can only see one direction - deleting a purpose shrinks the iteration and stays green. So the arm builds the SERVED set from what actually resolves and asserts set-equality with the advertised roster, plus `served.size === LAUNCH_PURPOSES.length` and `> 1` so a sweep that silently yielded zero cases cannot pass. Every resolved environment is asserted to be a member of ENVIRONMENT_NAMES.

(c) CODING SEAT - TWO ARMS, NOT ONE. First pins the COUNT (`Object.keys(delivered)` has length 0, not truthiness - `{}` and `{DATABASE_URL:...}` are both objects), plus `environment === null`, plus that no environment's value is among the values, plus that the launch-site convenience `launchDelivery` answers `undefined` since that is what the real call sites use. Second is strictly stronger: `vi.spyOn(delivery, "readEnvironmentDelivery")` asserts the read is NEVER CALLED, so there is no path from a coding-seat launch to plaintext at all rather than merely an empty result.

(d) REFUSALS PIN CODE **AND** LAYER, THREE ARMS - never merely "it failed". Absent credential -> ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE @ KEY. WRONG credential -> the SAME code and layer, which is the designed behaviour (splitting them would let a caller probe whether a credential is missing or merely incorrect, a fact about the secret). Off-roster purpose -> ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN @ SCOPE. This matters because the resolver has TWO refusing layers: an arm asserting only `ok: false` would stay green if the KEY path started answering what the SCOPE guard should. The SCOPE arm also asserts `LAUNCH_PURPOSES` does NOT contain "DEPLOY", so if that member is ever added this arm fails and forces the roster arm to be re-read instead of silently widening.

(e) NO RAW ERROR DATA. A Proxy over the real store makes `readEvents` THROW with `store read failed: SENTINEL_FROM_A_STORE_ERROR_MESSAGE`. Asserts the rostered code+layer AND that the sentinel is absent from `JSON.stringify(resolved)` - over the SERIALISED refusal rather than the fields a reader thought to check, so a message relayed into a `detail`, a `cause` or a field added later is still caught. `launchDelivery` on the same world answers `undefined`.

(b) CLOSED ALLOWLIST STILL GOVERNS THE HOST HALF, asserted against the PRODUCTION surface `agentEnvironment(host, delivered)` - not a helper reimplementing it. Non-allowlisted ambient HOST_ONLY_SECRET is absent from both the value and `Object.keys`; the operator's arbitrary DATABASE_URL arrives. Plus a COLLISION arm: an operator variable named `PATH` (the store's grammar admits it) does NOT displace the allowlisted runtime `PATH`.

A TEST BUG I HIT AND FIXED, worth recording because it would have made two arms vacuous: `seededWorld(null)` could not seed at all - seeding is itself a credentialled write, so a null-credential config stores NOTHING and the refusal arms would have been asserting against an EMPTY store rather than an underivable key. Split into `unkeyedWorld(credential)`, which seeds with a working credential FIRST and swaps the thunk afterwards. The failure surfaced because `seed()` asserts its own write succeeded - the vacuity guard did its job.

implementationPlan.description:
THE REAL CHILD-PROCESS CANARY (DoD 3) - `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-delivery-canary.test.ts`. A unit test cannot discharge this clause: DoD 3 asks for "a real child-process canary in the production composition path".

Plant a canary VALUE for a selected environment, launch a real child through the PRODUCTION composition path (a boundary step 3 actually wired), and have the child report whether it received the value - by exit code or a written file, NOT by echoing it to stdout, because stdout is captured into logs and that would defeat the sweep below.

THEN ASSERT THE BYTES ARE VALUE-FREE: the wrapper's output, any log line, and the receipt contain NO occurrence of the canary. DoD 3 requires both halves and each is useless alone - proving receipt without the sweep proves a leak is possible, and sweeping without proving receipt proves nothing at all (the canary may never have been delivered).

ASSERT THE NEGATIVE TOO: launch a CODING SEAT through its production path with the same canary configured and assert the child does NOT receive it.
